blindSummary:
This state/province led the national LGBT+ fatality count for four consecutive years (2021: 10 recorded violent deaths). In 2025, at least 15 hate crimes were recorded; a running total of 460 unresolved hate-crime cases was reported in January 2025. Activists cite deliberate filing and archiving of cases; the state/province's prosecutor's office has lost investigative files entirely. Emblematic cases have arrests but no final sentences. The 2025 murder of a man at a motel in a town in the state/province continued the pattern, with the state/provincial observatory counting 9 hate crimes earlier that same year.

The only institutional counterweight is recent: this state/province passed its gender-identity civil-code reform in 2025 (no age limit), the second-to-last of the 22 states/provinces to legislate it. Before that, a visitor or resident had no legal route to correct documents. The absence of any functioning investigation or prosecution machinery — distinct from other states/provinces where laws exist but enforcement is weak — makes the impunity here total.

Well below the national average. Compared with a neighbouring state/province that also carries sustained violence but has a comprehensive diversity law and a court-forced recognition procedure, this state/province's four-year lethality record combined with explicit case-archiving and lost files represents the worst enforcement climate. And compared with the state/province that typified the offence first in the country, this state/province's legal framework arrived latest and is least functional.
